r7-cannot-fail-sweep.title: Sweep for a THIRD check-that-cannot-fail
r7-cannot-fail-sweep.imperative: The handoff commissions this: sweep render.py's reported fields and the three new tests for a count, flag or assertion whose value is identical in the healthy and the defective world. Prove any candidate by mutation, not by reading.
r7-cannot-fail-sweep.finding: FOUND, with a mutation proof. The third instance is the FIXED FIELD ITSELF. render.py:436 defines pages as sum(1 for _ in out.rglob('*.md')) over the very tree it describes, so the number is now tautologically true of that tree and can therefore reveal nothing about it. Proved by mutation, not by reading: N8 (delete every second entity page immediately after writing it) leaves all 17 tests in tests/test_code_map.py GREEN, including test_render_report_page_count_equals_the_files_on_disk; N4 (never write any module INDEX.md - 112 pages in the real corpus) also leaves all 17 GREEN. Every mutation was asserted applied and render.py was restored byte-identical (sha256 match, 0 MUTATION PROBE strings). So B2's original complaint - 'a page is silently lost and the count that would reveal it cannot fail' - is NOT closed; the tautology moved from the writes to the tree. Two things make this a blocker rather than an observation. (1) tests/test_code_map.py:127-131 SHIPS the opposite claim: 'pages in the render report has to be a number that can be WRONG'. (2) tc18 tells g1 that entity_pages is 'a one-line fix in the same function', and the one-line fix matching g0's own precedent is to count the tree again - which would produce a second tautological field while g1 believes the family is closed. CONSTRUCTIVE: the report already carries a check that CAN fail and nobody runs it. Measured on a fresh build at HEAD: modules=112, pages=3648, entity_pages=3536, entity pages on disk=3535. pages - 1 - modules = 3535, which contradicts entity_pages=3536 by exactly the lost Verdict page. The falsifiable invariant is already in the artifact.

consolidation.summary: BLOCK on one finding, B3. B1 and B2 are both genuinely closed and every figure in the handoff's evidence table reproduced in my own hands: M1 and M2 mutation proofs both RED then restored byte-identical, 0 of 3535 entity-page headers carry a position over a full rebuild at HEAD, report pages=3648 against 3648 .md on disk, and the full suite 1709 passed / 2 skipped / 0 failed in a cleared environment. Every constraint held. B3 is the third cannot-fail sibling the handoff asked me to hunt: render.py:436 defines pages as a count of the tree it describes, so the tautology moved from the writes to the tree rather than being removed - mutation N8 deletes a quarter of the page tree and N4 deletes every module index page, and all 17 tests stay GREEN both times. It blocks for two reasons, neither requiring a render.py change: tests/test_code_map.py:127-131 ships the claim that pages 'has to be a number that can be WRONG', which is now false; and tc18 tells g1 that entity_pages is a one-line fix in the same function, inviting g1 to count the tree again and record the family as closed. The constructive close is already in the artifact - pages - 1 - modules = 3535 contradicts entity_pages = 3536 by exactly the lost Verdict page, a falsifiable invariant the report carries and nothing asserts. Six triage candidates flagged. REVIEW_RESULT at .agent-work/issue-456/crew-handoffs/g0-rereview-RESULT.md.

triage_candidates.statement: The rendered map's OUTPUT LAYOUT has no guard at all. render.py:22-26 documents map/<dotted.module>/<Entity>.md, map/<dotted.module>/INDEX.md and map/INDEX.md as the committed contract every consumer navigates by. Mutation N5 rewrote render.py:414 to write every entity page flat into map/ instead of its module directory and all 17 tests in tests/test_code_map.py stayed GREEN, including both new ones - because 'pages' counts .md files anywhere under the tree and the format tests read whatever pages they find. The two-tier index (g4) and the skills' Map-entry-point instruction (gs) both depend on this layout. Route to g1, whose charter is a check stage that can fail: assert the RELATIVE PATH of each page, not just its existence.

tc18 as filed is scoped narrower than the defect it names. It says entity_pages carries the identical cannot-fail shape and calls it 'a one-line fix in the same function'. But the root is the 'sizes' list, which is appended once per emit() CALL, and sizes feeds THREE report fields, not one: entity_pages (len(sizes)), median_entity_page_lines (sizes[len(sizes)//2][0]) and largest_5 (sizes[:5]). A one-line fix to entity_pages leaves the other two describing pages that may not exist on disk - largest_5 can name a key whose page was overwritten. Widen tc18 to name the list rather than the field, and record the invariant that CAN fail: pages - 1 - modules == distinct entity pages. Measured at HEAD that invariant already FAILS by exactly the lost Verdict page (3648 - 1 - 112 = 3535 vs entity_pages 3536).

The position guard is tied to ONE SPELLING of a position. tests/test_code_map.py:123 defines POSITION = re.compile(r'\.py:\d+'). Mutation N1 re-emitted the position as 'pkg/thing.py#L12' and all 17 tests stayed GREEN, because the regex needs a colon and test_page_header_keeps_the_file_path_and_the_entity_size passes on the path prefix. The confirmed ruling is 'nothing committed carries a position', not 'nothing carries a colon-form position'. Route to g1 or gb: express the guard as the property the consumer computes - a page header must be derivable from data that does not move when unrelated source moves - or at minimum widen the pattern to the position spellings a renderer would plausibly emit.

A count of the map, written into a file the map maps, changes the count it states - and this has already bitten once. tc21 and the shipped docstring at tests/test_code_map.py:180-184 both say a blunt position scan of the page tree returns TWO hits. A fresh build at HEAD returns THREE: the two real ones from test_checklist_engine.py's docstring, plus that very docstring, echoed onto map/tests.test_code_map/RenderedPageFormatTests.md:26. The claim falsified itself by being written. This repo maps its own tests, so the general rule for the remaining ten gates is: never state a corpus figure inside a mapped source file, and pin every figure in prose to the revision it was measured at (global-everyone.md 'Pin a claim to the revision you read it at'). gb, which commits every threshold, is where this needs to be doctrine.

Triage-id collision: 'tc17' currently names TWO different findings. spine.json:790 tc17 is the Verdict/verdict page collision routed to g1. execute.json:223 and :244 say the r6-fowler survey-postcondition engine defect was 'Refiled as tc17'. g1's residual risk from BOTH g0 blockers is routed by that id, so a reader who resolves it to the wrong record loses the collision finding. Also worth noting: .agent-work/issue-456/triage-candidates/ is EMPTY - every candidate actually lives in spine.json's triage_candidates array. A reviewer or a later gate looking in the directory named for them finds nothing and could reasonably conclude none were filed. I nearly did.

Heads-up for gs, not a defect: the untracked map/ tree sitting on disk right now was built by the PRE-FIX renderer and 3523 of its 3635 pages still carry a .py:<line> (grep -rlE '\.py:[0-9]+' map/ | wc -l = 3523; 3524 total hits). gs-implement's imperative does say 'Generate and commit the map tree', so a rebuild is obliged and B1 will not ship - but anyone who greps the on-disk tree before that rebuild will read B1 as unfixed, and a gs implementer who stages the existing tree instead of regenerating it would commit 3523 positions against a human-confirmed ruling. Worth one explicit line in the gs handoff: rebuild first, then stage.
